nodes.name: Electrodeposition of CoFe LDH
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH served as the anode catalyst, fabricated via single-step electrodeposition on nickel foam substrates (synthetic details provided in SI). SEM imaging confirmed uniform growth of rigid nanosheets across the three-dimensional scaffold, providing abundant exposed active sites while synergistically facilitating mass transport. EDS elemental mapping verified homogeneous dispersion of Co, Fe, and O on the surface, revealing a Co/Fe atomic ratio of 12.76. HRTEM analysis identified characteristic interplanar spacings at 0.247 nm and 0.280 nm, corresponding to (104) and (101) crystallographic planes of CoFe LDH, respectively. XPS elucidated the valence states.
nodes.source_text: In this work, the CoFe LDH served as the anode catalyst, fabricated via single-step electrodeposition on nickel foam substrates, and the synthetic details are provided in the SI.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co3+ peaks at 780.89 eV (2p3/2) and 796.52 eV (2p1/2), Co2+ at 782.23 eV (2p3/2) and 797.96 eV (2p1/2) with satellites; Fe 2p shows Fe2+ (712.55 eV, 723.70 eV), Fe3+ (715.44 eV, 726.30 eV), satellite (719.60 eV), Fe2+ is 24.7% of iron species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p spectrum resolved dual oxidation states: Co3+ peaks at 780.89 eV (2p3/2) and 796.52 eV (2p1/2) and Co2+ signatures at 782.23 eV (2p3/2) and 797.96 eV (2p1/2), both with satellite features (Sat.). Deconvolution of the Fe 2p spectrum revealed three components: Fe2+ (712.55 eV and 723.70 eV), Fe3+ (715.44 eV and 726.30 eV), and a satellite peak (719.60 eV), with Fe2+ constituting 24.7% of the iron species based on peak area integration.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) via CV at varying scan rates reveals CoFe LDH possesses the largest active interface of 33.0 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface area is reflected by the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) via cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves at varying scan rates, revealing that the CoFe LDH possesses the largest active interface (33.0 cm²), as shown in Fig. S7.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 550 h stability test, Co and Fe leaching rates were 29.1% and 34.0% respectively; without buffer at 1.0 A cm-2, after 1 h retention was 57.1% Co and 32.8% Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Even after 550 h, the leaching rates of Co and Fe were only 29.1% and 34.0%, which explains the maintained catalytic activity.
